  Council Member Dotson:

  Council Member Dotson commented this issue is a difficult one and the City
  Council is trying their best to be as fair as possible. He also commented that the
  Council understands both sides and a fair decision that works best for the City
  will be made. He thanked the Congresswoman Waters and her husband for
  coming out.

  Council Member Padilla:

  Council Member Padilla commented the issue of rent control is a very complex
  one. He stated at his recent event, many landlords and renters came up to him
  expressing their concerns. He also stated that he understands both sides, and the
  City Council will make the right decision for the City of Inglewood. He thanked
  everyone for coming out.

  Council Member Franklin:

  Council Member Franklin thanked everyone that came out to express their
  concerns. He also stated Ms. Marlo comments hits home for him. He liked that
  she commented that the City Council should look into relocation fees being based
  on longevity of a tenant. He also commented that he like Mr. Bennett’s comment
  regarding annual inflation adjustments is a critical point particularly when
  property taxes go up on an average of 2.1%, and he stated that the City Council
  should weigh in on this. Council Member Franklin also raised concerns regarding
  Section 8 housing regarding rate increase being passed on by to a tenant (found to

  5
 April 16, 2019

  be illegal). Council Member Franklin stated that he also raises concerns
  regarding the public hearing that might involve Seniors 62 and over, disabled and
  mental ill individuals and individuals with hardships that states that they need to
  raise the rent up to 8%, he suggested that the City Council might need staff
  personnel that will concentrate particularly on housing the phone calls,
  correspondence that will take place, and the research required before the public
  hearing take place.

  Council Member Morales:

  Council Member Morales thanked the property owners for coming out and sated
  that the Council understands that some property owners have sacrificed to get a
  property for their family, and it is appreciated. He also stated that the Mayor put
  together a fair proposal, and no one will be 100% happy when it’s all done, but
  the City Council will do their best to come up with a fair decision. He
  commented that some things he heard today from the public did stand out and
  should be taken into consideration. He stated that if a landlord is charging below
  80% of Market value they can appeal to go up 8% with no trigger to offer a
  relocation fee; which was well thought out, the single family homes and unit
  below 4 unit apartments that were left out are things that are starting to look more
  reasonable. He also commented that he hopes the Mayor considers the issue of
  major repairs or major remodeling to an apartment building, and how it will be
  feasible, but allowing it to trigger a reasonable increase so that the residents can
  benefit from the remodeling. Council Member Morales stated an owner
  commented that it seems like the rent stabilization is taking from the owners with
  nothing in return but it isn’t true because the increase value that has happened in
  the last four of five years to property is the specific benefit that was taking by the
  City of Inglewood, its residents, and every economic boost that the city has had
  and the owners are the biggest benefactors of it. He also commented that he
  appreciates the fact that the Mayor included an additional amount to disabled
  renters as well as seniors. He stated that the Mayor had a well thought out
  process because even if the City Council does a sliding scale based on a trigger
  that is for disabled tenants and seniors to benefit another boost. He commented
  that he supports the Mayor by moving forward to the City Attorney’s office but he
  would like to do it with the expectation that the City Council’s comments be
  thought through and included.

  Mayor Butts:

  Mayor Butts commented that he agrees with the comments made by Council
  Member Morales, and Council Member Padilla. He commented that the
  Moratorium is not all one way for tenants. He stated that there are some
  properties that have gone up 150% in the last seven years. He stated that the
  reason for the increase on property is because the Council has stabilized the
  finances for the city, infrastructure has been renewed, streets residential and
  boulevard are different, tree trimming which helps to increase the value of the
  property, and it’s the tax dollars that do that. He also stated that there is a definite
  benefit for people who own property here. He also stated that a property owners
  building is worth what the city is worth, and collectively the Council has done a
  good job renewing the city. Mayor Butts stated when it comes down to those that
  rent, the reality is when rent gets too high, you have to find somewhere else to
  rent (if you choose to rent). He also stated that the Council has to modify their
  thinking when it comes to that. Mayor Butts stated that there’s a social cost to
  raising the rent unreasonably and he doesn’t believe that any of the landlords
  sitting in the audience raises rent unreasonably. He stated that Public meetings
  are being held such as this one, and there has been plenty participation. He also
  stated that he and Melanie are going to go back and look into amortization cost
  because the City of Los Angeles allows a landlord that has to, for example, place
  a roof on their property, a temporary surcharge is allowed to put on the rent to
  amortize 50% of the cost which is fair however, the city doesn’t want to become
  the arbitrator. Mayor Butts commented that the city is trying to draft something
  that is rule based. He stated that he heard the landlord when they said 9 months

  6
 April 16, 2019

  may be too soon to get a 100% relocation allowance, and the City Council will
  consider that.
  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales that the
  City Council does hereby extend the Moratorium for 60 more days to allow him
  and his assistant and the City
  Attorney to fine tune the Ordinance. The motion was carried by the following roll
  call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales that the
  City Council does hereby authorize the Mayor to work with the City Attorney to
  work on behalf of the City Council bearing in mind the Brown Act would
  preclude a number of the City Council being involved and to bring back a final
  Ordinance within the 60 days if possible, and if they are unable to finish the
  Ordinance within 60 days to consider extending the Moratorium even further; but
  the objective is to come back in 60 days with an Ordinance, for the City Council
  to vote up or down. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
